nodes.description: Immune-mediated destruction of blood cells is the commonest autoimmune manifestation, reported in every published patient series. The individual lineages affected - Coombs-positive haemolytic anaemia, immune thrombocytopenia and autoimmune neutropenia - are recorded in the OMIM clinical synopsis for this disease but are not named in any abstract that can be quoted here, so this entry binds the finding at the level its sources state it.

nodes.description: Four cryo-EM structures of full-length human DOCK11 show that activated CDC42 engages a distal armadillo-repeat site separate from the catalytic domain, driving DOCK11 to the plasma membrane and raising its exchange rate. DOCK11 is therefore a switch with gain, and below a threshold the loop does not ignite at all. This is the structural reason a missense allele that only reduces protein can cause disease as severe as a null allele.

evidence.snippet: DOCK11 predominantly adopts a U-shaped dimer that binds to nucleotide-free Cdc42 via the catalytic domain, whereas activated Cdc42 engages a distal site within the armadillo-repeat domain.

nodes.description: The germline knockout has a reduced splenic marginal zone B cell fraction and a conditional knockout shows the requirement is B-cell intrinsic. T cells from a Dock11 knockout reproduce the overt activation and proinflammatory cytokine output seen in patient T cells.

A dock11-knockout zebrafish reproduces both the anaemia and the abnormal red cell morphology seen in patients, and the anaemia is rescued by ectopic expression of constitutively active CDC42, which places the defect downstream of failed CDC42 activation. The cell-intrinsic mechanism in human erythroblasts has not been established.

evidence.snippet: Anemia and aberrant erythrocyte morphologic features were recapitulated in a newly generated dock11-knockout zebrafish model, and anemia was amenable to rescue on ectopic expression of constitutively active CDC42.

nodes.description: DOCK11's catalytic DOCKER (DHR-2) domain loads GTP onto CDC42, and it does so for CDC42 specifically rather than for the related GTPases TC10 and TCL. Patient cells show impaired CDC42 activation whichever allele class they carry.

evidence.reference_title: Zizimin2: a novel, DOCK180-related Cdc42 guanine nucleotide exchange factor expressed predominantly in lymphocytes.
evidence.snippet: Zizimin2 and zizimin1 have similar primary structures and both proteins bound and activated Cdc42 but not the Cdc42-related proteins TC10 or TCL.

nodes.description: Sub-threshold CDC42-GTP leaves CDC42-dependent actin nucleation unsupported. Patient T cells form no filopodia and migrate abnormally, and activated patient T cells and B-lymphoblastoid lines show aberrant protrusions and abnormal speed in confined channels with altered actin polymerisation. Knocking DOCK11 down in healthy donor cells reproduces both.

nodes.description: Immunoglobulin replacement for the antibody deficiency, with antibiotic prophylaxis, aimed at preventing the recurrent pneumonia that accumulates into irreversible bronchiectasis.
